title: Reading Lines

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: In this lesson you will learn how to read a file one line at a time with a for loop.
idea: You can loop over a file: for line in f:. Each turn gives you one line of text (often with a newline at the end). line.strip() removes extra spaces and newlines so printing looks tidy.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change print(line.strip()) to print("Line:", line.strip()). Press Run.

practice.text: Loop over tips.txt and print each line stripped.
practice.hint: Inside the for loop, print line.strip() so each tip shows without extra newline junk at the end.
practice.starterTip: Replace print() with print(line.strip()) — indented under for line in f:.
practice.starter:
f = open("tips.txt")
for line in f:
    print()
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if both tip lines print using a for loop over the file.

practice.text: Count how many lines are in scores.txt and print the count.
practice.hint: The loop already adds 1 each time you visit a line. After f.close(), print the count variable.
practice.starterTip: Use print(count) at the end — scores.txt has three lines, so you should see 3.
practice.starter:
count = 0
f = open("scores.txt")
for line in f:
    count = count + 1
f.close()
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if count is 3 and printed.

quiz.question: What does for line in f: give you each turn?

options.text: The whole file as one blob only
One line of text from the file

quiz.correct: Looping a file visits one line at a time.
quiz.wrong: Each iteration is the next line.

quiz.question: Why use strip() on a line?

options.text: To remove leftover newlines and spaces

quiz.correct: strip() cleans edges of the string.
quiz.wrong: Lines often end with \n; strip removes it.

quiz.question: When should you close the file after a line loop?

options.text: Only if there is an error

quiz.correct: Close when you are done reading.
